news_drafts.headline: Council tax increase effectiveness eroded: 19.5% of any rise lost to Council Tax Reduction Scheme costs
news_drafts.lead: The council's ability to raise revenue through council tax is severely constrained by welfare support costs it must fund. This income source is less reliable and lower-yielding than assumed by councils elsewhere.

news_drafts.headline: School reserves depleted from £20M to £6M in four years, requiring continued council subsidy

findings.headline: Council tax increase effectiveness eroded: 19.5% of any rise lost to Council Tax Reduction Scheme costs
findings.detail: Proposed 4% council tax increase generates £1.429M additional income per 1% increase but costs £0.278M in additional Council Tax Reduction Scheme (CTRS) support, netting only £1.151M per 1% increase. This means nearly 1 in 5 council tax revenue is diverted to subsidizing bills for lower-income households. The paper notes 42% of RCT properties are in Band A (lowest band).
findings.matters: The council's ability to raise revenue through council tax is severely constrained by welfare support costs it must fund. This income source is less reliable and lower-yielding than assumed by councils elsewhere.
findings.figures: 1% Council Tax increase gross: £1.429M; CTRS cost: £0.278M; net: £1.151M; leakage: 19.5%; Band A properties: 42% of RCT housing stock
findings.quote: A 1% increase in Council Tax will generate an additional income for the Council of £1.429M (at the 2026/27 tax base level) but will also cost £0.278M in additional CTRS requirements. It therefore follows that a 1% increase generates a net additional income of £1.151M, or stated another way, 19.5% of any Council Tax increase is lost to support the increased costs associated with Welsh Government's CTRS.

findings.headline: School reserves depleted from £20M to £6M in four years, requiring continued council subsidy
findings.detail: School aggregate balances collapsed from £20M (March 2022) to £6M (March 2025), a 70% drawdown. Schools received significant one-off Welsh Government resources and were 'previously advised to use their reserves responsibly.' The council is now allocating full inflationary funding plus £1M for ALN/special school capacity (5.6% cash increase in ISB). Schools budget increased 45% over 10 years vs 32% for other services, representing £18.6M extra allocation.
findings.matters: School reserves cannot buffer future cost pressures. The council is now committed to protecting school budgets, which limits flexibility elsewhere and signals structural cost pressures in demand-led services.
findings.figures: School balances: £20M (2021/22) → £6M (31 March 2025); ISB increase 2026/27: £12.005M (5.6%); ALN enhancement: £1M; 10-year ISB increase 45% vs other services 32% (£18.6M differential)
findings.quote: For context, the aggregate level of school balances increased from £2M to £20M over the course of the financial years 2020/21 and 2021/22 and have now reduced to £6M at the 31st March 2025.

findings.headline: Single-year settlement with no forward visibility creates medium-term budget planning uncertainty
findings.detail: Welsh Government provided only a single-year settlement for 2026/27 with no indication of future year funding levels. The final settlement improved to 4.5% only after a budget agreement that included £112.8M nationally for local government. The council notes 'The settlement provides no indication of future year settlement levels.' This follows a pattern of provisional, then final settlements, making MTFP forecasting speculative.
findings.matters: Without forward visibility, councils cannot plan debt repayment, capital programmes, or service restructuring with confidence. Single-year certainty forces repeated emergency budget cycles.
findings.figures: 2026/27 settlement increase: 2.7% provisional (24 Nov 2025), improved to 4.5% final (20 Jan 2026 after £112.8M national top-up); settlement range across Wales 4.1% to 6.1%
findings.quote: The settlement provides no indication of future year settlement levels.

findings.headline: Efficiency savings approaching exhaustion point with increasing impact on frontline services
findings.detail: The council has delivered £40M+ in efficiency and service reconfiguration measures over three years. Senior leadership now explicitly states that 'following the delivery of over £40M of efficiency measures over the last 3 years... it is becoming increasingly difficult to deliver such opportunities without impacting on front line services.' The 2026/27 efficiency target of £6.335M is identified as increasingly challenging to achieve.
findings.matters: Once a council exhausts efficiency savings, the only levers left are service cuts, borrowing, or further tax rises. This signals a tightening financial straitjacket for future years.
findings.figures: £40M+ efficiency measures over 3 years; £6.335M target for 2026/27 (from: General Efficiencies £3.031M, Non-Pay Freeze £0.976M, Restructuring £1.265M, External Funding £1.063M)
findings.quote: following the delivery of over £40M of efficiency measures over the last 3 years, as part of us balancing the largest budget gaps we have ever experienced as a Council, it is becoming increasingly difficult to deliver such opportunities without impacting on front line services.

findings.headline: Three consecutive years of unprecedented budget gaps now forcing reliance on transitional reserves
findings.detail: The council faced £36M budget gaps annually for the last three years. For 2026/27, after efficiency measures and council tax increases, they still need £0.911M from reserves to balance, reducing their transitional reserve from £4.745M to £3.834M. The deputy Chief Executive notes this 'does not deal with the underlying recurring budget issue into the future.'
findings.matters: A lender needs to know whether a council can sustain service delivery and debt repayment when it requires reserve drawdowns every year and savings are becoming harder to find without affecting frontline services.
findings.figures: £36M annual gap × 3 years; £6.335M efficiencies delivered 2026/27; £0.911M reserve drawdown; £40M+ total efficiencies over 3 years
findings.quote: Over the last 3 financial years our budget strategies have had to address the largest budget gaps this Council has ever faced at around £36M for each year.
